message.content: {"1904_8353802248403": {"answer": "B", "reason": "The enlargement of the left upper mediastinum (indicated by the arrow) combined with left ventricular prominence and symptoms of hypoxaemia is characteristic of a persistent left superior vena cava draining into the left atrium, creating a right-to-left shunt."}, "1904_8353802248805": {"answer": "C", "reason": "The specific combination of a widened left superior mediastinum and mild hypoxaemia strongly suggests a persistent left superior vena cava draining directly into the left atrium, causing deoxygenated blood to bypass the lungs."}, "1904_8353802248955": {"answer": "C", "reason": "The radiographic finding of a prominent left superior mediastinal shadow in a patient with unexplained hypoxaemia is most consistent with a persistent left superior vena cava draining into the left atrium."}}
